works.title: 6,500 Alphabets Make a Map
works.rationale: The documented production process is a dome installation assembled from 6,500 digitized human-authored pictographs, syllabaries and ideographs; there is no generative model in the pipeline at all, let alone model-generated output fed back as training input across generations. The work reconceptualizes 'algorithm' as an epistemic proposal, which is thematization rather than any recursive training loop. Under Step 2 of the criterion it can only be a reference (and even the reference to model collapse specifically is at best oblique).

works.title: AI Delivered: The Abject
works.rationale: The exhibition contains GAN-trained films, a live dialogue-generating website, and a counter-intelligence machine, all deployed to probe where AI competence breaks down. Nothing in the described production process indicates that any of these systems was trained on model-generated outputs, and no second training generation of a continuous pipeline is documented. GAN training on undisclosed (presumably real) data plus live generation is single-generation use; the collapse/abjection theme is probed and depicted, not enacted as recursive training, so Step 2 applies.

works.title: Cybernetics, or Ghosts?
works.rationale: This is an anthology of fifteen human writers responding in fiction to Calvino's 1967 essay, plus a companion album, using the generative-AI moment as a thematic mirror. The production pipeline is entirely human-authored writing and music; no generative model training of any kind is described, and therefore no model-generation-to-model-generation loop exists. It discusses and alludes to the generative-AI moment, which is squarely the 'references' bucket.

works.title: En attendant le récit / Tales of Narrativelessness
works.rationale: Three chatbots converse live in a loop restarting every seven minutes; each model consumes the others' generated text, but only as conversational context at inference time. The criterion requires model-generated output to be fed back as TRAINING input for a subsequent generation of the pipeline, and nothing in the description indicates any retraining — the models are pre-existing (ChatGPT, Claude, Mistral) and the loop is a restaged, unscripted dialogue. A looping inference performance about AI anxiety and the end of grand narratives depicts recursive machine self-reference without instantiating recursive training, so Step 2 applies.

works.title: Ent- (non-earthly delights)
works.rationale: The work is a physical sculpture with AR layers staging Bosch as a warning about quantum-accelerated AI surveillance, with 'sliming' framed as resistance to detection systems. The documented production process involves no generative model training at all, and thus no possibility of a model-generated-output-to-training loop across generations. It thematizes and critiques AI systems, which under Step 2 is reference only.

works.title: Errorism
works.rationale: Kurant feeds her own writings — human-authored material — into GPT-2 and GPT-3 and renders the output as a holographic animation. This is precisely the case the criterion pre-empts by name: training (or conditioning) on human-authored material, 'even the artist's own prior writing,' without a demonstrable model-generation-to-model-generation loop is references only. The loop described is human-text-in, model-output-out, rendered once; the catalog text's own characterization of it as a 'demonstration of the recursive self-consumption/collapse dynamic' is an interpretive gloss, not evidence that model output re-entered training for a subsequent generation. One pass through two separate models does not constitute two generations of a continuous pipeline.

works.title: Hallucinations of an Artifact
works.rationale: Dancers improvise alongside a generative-AI avatar to invent speculative lives for a bronze statue, using the model as a live collaborator. The description documents inference-time generation in performance, not any training step, and certainly not training on the model's own prior outputs across two generations. The work uses and depicts generative AI (and its hallucinatory character) without any documented recursive training loop, so Step 2 applies.

works.title: Matrix Vegetal
works.rationale: A video installation braiding plant-healing practices with 'quantum-inspired' technology treats non-Western epistemics as a knowledge register alongside computation. No generative model, no training of any kind, and no feedback of model output into training is described in the production process. This is thematic and depictive engagement only; the connection even to the model-collapse mechanism is not evident from the text, but in any case Step 2 yields references only.

works.title: Mythmachine
works.rationale: The AI-driven biome 'listens to and choreographs itself from ambient audio feedback captured live in the gallery.' The feedback here is environmental, real-time input driving behavior — an inference-time responsiveness loop — not model-generated output fed back as training data for a subsequent generation of a generative pipeline. Even if the installation's own sounds are part of the ambient audio, no retraining across generations is documented, and the input is mixed live gallery audio rather than a demonstrable model-to-model training chain. The work proposes alternative intelligences as critique of extractive ML, which is thematization under Step 2.

works.title: The Feral: Epoch 1
works.rationale: The described mechanism is successive human artists 'feeding' one AI across 32 generations of artists over 1,000 years — the generational relay is human, and the training input is artist-provided material, which the criterion explicitly classifies as human-authored input without a model-generation-to-model-generation loop. Nothing in the text states that the AI's own generated outputs re-enter its training, and as 'Epoch 1' only the first chapter exists, so even a planned recursion would not yet be demonstrable across two generations. The project thematizes machine learning across time rather than instantiating recursive self-consumption; Step 2 applies.

works.title: The Next Biennial Should Be Curated by a Machine
works.rationale: The AI is trained on real Biennial and Whitney archives — human-authored institutional material — and then generates fake biographies and press releases endlessly, live. Continuous generation is not continuous retraining: nothing in the description indicates the hallucinated outputs are fed back as training data for a subsequent model generation. This matches the criterion's Step 2 exactly: training on human-authored material without a demonstrable model-generation-to-model-generation loop, while enacting and exposing algorithmic curation's absurdity, is reference (here, a performative critique), not instantiation.

works.title: The Sleight of the Machine
works.rationale: An AI video model is used to generate a film whose characteristic failures (multiplying hands, physics violations) are deliberately retained as the content. This is single-generation use of a generative model with the glitches curated as evidence; the production process as described involves no feeding of model output back into training for a subsequent generation. Making generative failure visible depicts and thematizes the model's degradation modes without instantiating the recursive training mechanism, so Step 2 applies.

works.title: Thousand Lives (BOB lineage)
works.rationale: The work is a live, indefinitely running neurosymbolic agent whose turtle continuously updates its beliefs — an executing inferential system exhibited as artwork. Belief-updating within a running simulation is inference/state-update, not generative-model training, and the description gives no indication that model-generated outputs are used as training data for a subsequent generation of a generative pipeline. While the system does continuously consume its own simulated experience, that is a different loop from the model-collapse mechanism the criterion specifies; without any documented recursive training generations, Step 2 yields references only (and the work arguably does not even reference collapse so much as autonomous inference).

works.title: V3: Model Collapse
works.rationale: The documented production structure is a four-part project in which 'each exhibition's own photographs and collages are fed back as training data for the next' — a continuous pipeline in which each exhibition is produced from a model trained on the previous exhibition's material, and the material of every exhibition after the first therefore derives from model output trained on prior model output. As the third chapter, V3 sits at least two feedback generations deep, satisfying the criterion's requirement of model-generated output demonstrably re-entering training across at least two generations of a continuous pipeline; the work is explicitly framed as literalizing model collapse as a visible, physically installed material process. The human mediation in each cycle (photographing, collaging, installing) is curation within the loop, analogous to the biased/curated sampling the technical literature's loops also include, and does not break the model-to-model training chain the text documents.

works.title: Wilding AI Lab
works.rationale: The lab publicly 'reopens the black box' of generative models, treating the training/generation process itself as artistic material inside a spatial-audio dome. Although actual training appears to occur as part of the practice, nothing in the description states or implies that model-generated outputs are fed back as training input for a subsequent generation — the data sources and pipeline topology described give no hint of recursion, and exposing or performing training is not the same as looping it. Working with training as material while not documenting any model-generation-to-model-generation loop falls under Step 2; this is engagement with and depiction of the training process rather than an ambiguous partial disclosure of a collapse loop.

papers.rationale: The abstract directly asserts and names the mechanism: 'use of model-generated content in training causes irreversible defects in the resulting models, where tails of the original content distribution disappear,' terming this Model Collapse. It claims the effect is shown across VAEs, Gaussian Mixture Models, and LLMs, with theoretical intuition for its ubiquity among learned generative models. This is an explicit affirmative demonstration-plus-theory claim that recursive training on model-generated data degrades generative models, i.e., the mechanism as described.

The abstract reports analytical and empirical analysis of autophagous (self-consuming) training loops in state-of-the-art image models and concludes that 'without enough fresh real data in each generation of an autophagous loop, future generative models are doomed to have their quality (precision) or diversity (recall) progressively decrease,' naming this Model Autophagy Disorder. This affirms the existence of progressive degradation under recursive training on model-generated data, with the important scoping condition that sufficient fresh real data per generation can avert it — a conditional that refines but does not contradict the mechanism as described.

Although the paper's headline contribution is that collapse is avoidable, its abstract explicitly confirms the mechanism's existence in the regime the original literature describes: 'We confirm that replacing the original real data by each generation's synthetic data does indeed tend towards model collapse,' empirically across model sizes, architectures, and data types, and analytically via the linear-model framework where test error grows with iterations under replacement. It then shows that accumulating real plus synthetic data bounds the error and prevents collapse. So the paper supports that the degradation mechanism exists as described under data replacement, while narrowing its claimed inevitability — a scope qualification, not a refutation.
